newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro rights watchdog rejects Sinn Fein's Adams.
newsitem.headline: Euro rights watchdog rejects Sinn Fein's Adams.

text.p: The European Commission on Human Rights on Friday rejected a complaint filed by Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams against the British government's refusal to allow him into mainland Britain in 1993.

The Strasbourg-based Council of Europe said in a statement that the Commission, which vets suits filed with the European Court of Human Rights, threw out complaints by Adams and British Labour parliamentarian Tony Benn, who had invited him to speak at the House of Commons.
British Home Secretary Michael Howard invoked the 1989 Prevention of Terrorism Act to bar Adams.
The leader of the Irish Republican Army's political wing argued that his right of self-expression had been violated and Benn that the ban violated his freedom of information.

However the Commission said the British government's decision was justified by the situation in Northern Ireland and the fact that Adams was considered close to the IRA, which is waging a guerrilla war to force Britain out of the province.

The Commission noted that the European Convention on Human Rights allowed freedom of expression to be restricted in the interests of national security. It also noted that Britain had not ratified a protocol to the convention on the free circulation of persons.
